messages:
mina: heads-up — onboarding run for horizon-18b-int4v4 with 64k prefill hit a repro where new writes land in recently-evicted slots. saw token drift starting ~60010. opening thread to collect notes.

ev an: can you drop the exact command and a minimal log snippet?

mina: command: ./onboard_eval.sh --model=horizon-18b-int4v4 --prefill=60400 --quant=int4v4 --trace=kv,evict
log excerpt: 
[2027-03-14T03:12:01Z] kv.write req=59990 stored=59990
[2027-03-14T03:12:01Z] kv.evict shrink_to=58400
[2027-03-14T03:12:01Z] kv.write req=60011 stored=58401  # write landed at evicted slot
[2027-03-14T03:12:01Z] kv.read  req=60011 served=58401
[2027-03-14T03:12:01Z] rotary.apply pos=60011 used=58401
[2027-03-14T03:12:01Z] gen token="that" prob_delta=0.021

tara: that looks like a classic base/head race: prefix-evict moved base and freed slots but writer computed slot against stale base. did you run single-threaded or with batching?

mina: single-threaded canary run but kernel uses async prefetcher that batches writes; still reproducible. i have a tiny repro harness that does deterministic bursts to hit the race.

chao: possible quick fixes: 1) writers verify base after mapping slot and retry if base changed (lockless retry), 2) make eviction update base and head under the same lock (safe but slower), 3) short-term: enable kv.repair-scan on canary to detect and abort on mismatch.

ev an: i prefer 1) if low overhead. sounds like earlier teams used the volatile-read+retry pattern for exactly this. can you prototype and measure retries metric?

mina: implementing write-then-verify-retry now. small patch in kv_shard fast-path. adding debug metric kv.write.retries and a dev-only assert when served_pos != req_pos during trace.

ci-bot: CI queued: horizon-int4v4/patch-3101112222. Running unit tests: kv-evict-race, kv-index-consistency, long-prefill-smoke.

tara: also audit sharding math for any uint16_t casts or POS_MASK uses. we've seen masks and casts cause aliasing at 16k/32k boundaries — different root but similar symptoms.

chao: another angle — if eviction is aggressive and prefetcher still holds references, we might see re-use of freed memory before zeroing. ensure evict path zeroes slots or increments an epoch counter per slot and writers write current epoch. easier: add slot.epoch check to reads.

mina: good point. i'll add epoch verification in read path as an optional dev check. also adding a micro-benchmark that repeatedly prefill->evict->burst-write to ensure no stale reads after fix.

ev an: once patch lands run a float32 vs int4 diff on the longprefill goldset with same seed to see if token-deltas vanish. please record per-token divergence histogram.

mina: will do. enabling kv.repair-scan=true on pool-canary-4 until we roll the patch. leaving traces enabled and saving diffs to /var/tmp/horizon-longprefill-diffs. :thumbsup:
